questions.prompt: After the city had been captured, the enemy withdrew from the walls.
questions.answer: Urbe captā hostēs ā moenibus excessērunt.

questions.prompt: With Caesar as leader, the soldiers crossed the river bravely.
questions.answer: Caesare duce mīlitēs flūmen fortiter trānsiērunt.

questions.prompt: When the signal had been given, the diligent general ordered an advance.
questions.answer: Signō datō dīligēns dux prōcēdere iussit.

questions.prompt: Since the enemy had been conquered, the citizens rejoiced greatly.
questions.answer: Hostibus victīs cīvēs magnopere gāvīsī sunt.

questions.prompt: With the winds blowing, the sailors set the white sails.
questions.answer: Ventīs flantibus nautae vēla alba dedērunt.

questions.prompt: After the auspices had been taken, the prince addressed the army.
questions.answer: Auspiciīs captīs princeps exercitum adlocūtus est.

questions.answer: Portā apertā turba in templum irrūpit.

questions.prompt: Although the leader was unwilling, the legions demanded battle.
questions.answer: Duce invītō legiōnēs proelium poposcērunt.

questions.prompt: When the letter had been read, the anxious mother wept.
questions.answer: Epistulā lēctā anxia māter flēvit.

questions.prompt: With the author speaking, everyone listened in silence.
questions.answer: Auctōre loquente omnēs silentiō audiēbant.

questions.prompt: After the gems had been counted, the king locked the treasury.
questions.answer: Gemmīs numerātīs rēx aerārium clausit.

questions.prompt: Since peace had been made, the weary soldiers returned home.
questions.answer: Pāce factā fessī mīlitēs domum revertērunt.

questions.prompt: With the sun having set, the shepherds drove the flocks home.
questions.answer: Sōle occāsō pāstōrēs gregēs domum ēgērunt.

questions.prompt: When the bridge had been destroyed, the enemy could not cross.
questions.answer: Ponte dēlētō hostēs trānsīre nōn potuērunt.

questions.prompt: With the doors closed, the philosopher taught his eager pupils.
questions.answer: Iānuīs clausīs philosophus discipulōs cupidōs docuit.

questions.answer: Duce interfectō exercitus victōrī sē dēdidit.

questions.prompt: With the gods willing, we shall conquer our fierce enemies.
questions.answer: Dīs volentibus ferōcēs hostēs vincēmus.

questions.answer: Agrīs vāstātīs famēs miserum populum pressit.

questions.prompt: Since the consul was in command, the state feared nothing.
questions.answer: Cōnsule praesente cīvitās nihil timēbat.

questions.prompt: After the walls had been built, the townsfolk feared no siege.
questions.answer: Mūrīs aedificātīs oppidānī nūllam obsidiōnem timuērunt.

questions.prompt: With the tyrant driven out, the citizens restored freedom.
questions.answer: Tyrannō expulsō cīvēs lībertātem restituērunt.

questions.answer: Tempestāte ortā nāvis in altō marī iactāta est.

questions.prompt: The wine having been drunk, the guests sang joyful songs.
questions.answer: Vīnō haustō convīvae laeta carmina cecinērunt.

questions.prompt: Since the leaders disagreed, the plan was abandoned.
questions.answer: Ducibus dissidentibus cōnsilium relictum est.

questions.prompt: When the general had been killed, the soldiers fled through the fields.
questions.answer: Duce interfectō, mīlitēs per agrōs fūgērunt.

questions.prompt: With the enemy conquered, the victorious army returned home.
questions.answer: Hostibus victīs, exercitus victor domum rediit.

questions.prompt: After the bridge had been destroyed, the horsemen could not cross the river.
questions.answer: Ponte dēlētō, equitēs flūmen trānsīre nōn potuērunt.

questions.prompt: With Caesar as leader, the legions endured every hardship.
questions.answer: Caesare duce, legiōnēs omnem labōrem tulērunt.

questions.prompt: When the truth had been discovered, the interpreter refuted the false witness.
questions.answer: Vēritāte cognitā, interpres testem falsum refellit.

questions.prompt: With her fillet torn away, the priestess loosened her hair.
questions.answer: Vittā dīvulsā, sacerdōs capillōs solvit.

questions.prompt: With their weapons sharpened, the soldiers awaited the gladiatorial contest.
questions.answer: Armīs acūtīs, mīlitēs certāmen gladiātōrium exspectāvērunt.

questions.prompt: Since the flattery had been rejected, the honest judge upheld the law.
questions.answer: Blanditiā repudiātā, iūdex probus lēgem affirmāvit.

questions.prompt: With the walls stormed, the women ran toward the shore.
questions.answer: Moenibus expugnātīs, mulierēs ad lītus cucurrērunt.

questions.prompt: With the child nursing, the weary mother sang a gentle song.
questions.answer: Īnfante lactente, māter fessa carmen lēne cecinit.

questions.prompt: Although the enemies had been torn apart, the war was not yet finished.
questions.answer: Hostibus dīvulsīs, bellum nōndum cōnfectum erat.

questions.prompt: While the leader was speaking, the whole crowd fell silent.
questions.answer: Duce dīcente, tōta multitūdō conticuit.

questions.prompt: When the gates had been opened, the citizens welcomed the returning victor.
questions.answer: Portīs apertīs, cīvēs victōrem redeuntem excēpērunt.

questions.prompt: Since the mind is rational, human beings crave the truth.
questions.answer: Mente ratiōnālī, hominēs vēritātem concupīscunt.

questions.prompt: With his cloak thrown aside, the old man stretched out his hands.
questions.answer: Pallā abiectā, senex manūs tetendit.

questions.prompt: After the signal had been given, the ships departed from the harbor.
questions.answer: Signō datō, nāvēs ex portū discessērunt.

questions.prompt: With their parent commanding, the boys obeyed without complaint.
questions.answer: Parente imperante, puerī sine querēlā pāruērunt.

questions.prompt: Although his arguments had been weakened, the orator did not give in.
questions.answer: Argūmentīs extenuātīs, ōrātor nōn concessit.

questions.prompt: With the fields laid waste, famine oppressed the wretched farmers.
questions.answer: Agrīs vāstātīs, famēs miserōs agricolās oppressit.

questions.prompt: When the auspices had been taken, the consul led out the army.
questions.answer: Auspiciīs captīs, cōnsul exercitum ēdūxit.

questions.prompt: After the temple had been built, the citizens praised the gods.
questions.answer: Templō aedificātō, cīvēs deōs laudāvērunt.

questions.prompt: When the commander had encouraged the soldiers, the battle began.
questions.answer: Imperātōre mīlitēs cohortātō, proelium coeptum est.
